title: Filtered 2-colimits are equivalences with $\mathcal C_\infty$
statement:
In the situation of [det-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit-model] (directed $I$, coherent normalized
cocone), let $\Phi\colon\mathcal C_\infty\to\mathcal D$ be the comparison functor. Then:

1. $\Phi$ is essentially surjective if and only if (Obj) holds;
2. $\Phi$ is full if and only if (Hom-surj) holds;
3. $\Phi$ is faithful if and only if (Hom-inj) holds.

Hence the cocone is a filtered 2-colimit ([det-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit-conditions]) if and only
if $\Phi$ is an equivalence of categories.

proof.text: By [det-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit-model], every object of $\mathcal C_\infty$ is a pair $(i,x)$ and $\Phi(i,x)=\Phi_i(x)$. Essential surjectivity therefore says exactly that every $d\in\mathcal D$ is isomorphic to some $\Phi_i(x)$, which is (Obj) in [det-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit-conditions]. The direction of the isomorphism is immaterial because it can be inverted.

Fix $a=(i,x)$ and $b=(j,y)$. The index $J_{ij}=\{k\in I:k\ge i,j\}$ in [det-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit-model] is a set, is nonempty by directedness, and any two indices have an upper bound still in $J_{ij}$. As a preorder it has at most one arrow between fixed objects, so it is a small filtered category. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] to its Hom diagram: every arrow $a\to b$ is $[k,g]$. The model gives
$$\Phi([k,g])=\theta_{jk,y}\Phi_k(g)\theta_{ik,x}^{-1}.$$
Thus, if $\Phi$ is full, a preimage of any $\varphi:\Phi_i(x)\to\Phi_j(y)$ has a representative giving exactly the equation in (Hom-surj) of [det-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit-conditions]. Conversely that condition supplies $[k,g]$ mapping to every such $\varphi$. Since all objects are pairs, this is fullness.

source.place: Blueprint step 2: representatives and fullness; Stacks Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits)

proof.text:
Assume (Hom-inj) of [det-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit-conditions]. For fixed $(i,x),(j,y)$, take arrows with equal $\Phi$-images. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise](1) write them as $[k,g]$ and $[l,h]$. Choose $m\ge k,l$ and put $u=t_{km}(g)$, $v=t_{lm}(h)$ using [det-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit-model]. They have the same classes as $g,h$. Since the comparison is a well-defined functor, equality of their images gives
$$\theta_{jm,y}\Phi_m(u)\theta_{im,x}^{-1}=\theta_{jm,y}\Phi_m(v)\theta_{im,x}^{-1}.$$
Cancel the outer isomorphisms to get $\Phi_m(u)=\Phi_m(v)$. Apply (Hom-inj) to the two arrows $u,v:T_{im}x\to T_{jm}y$ in $\mathcal C_m$: there is $n\ge m$ with $T_{mn}(u)=T_{mn}(v)$. Conjugating both sides by the same source and target associators gives
$$t_{mn}(u)=\tau_{jmn,y}T_{mn}(u)\tau_{imn,x}^{-1}=\tau_{jmn,y}T_{mn}(v)\tau_{imn,x}^{-1}=t_{mn}(v).$$
The equality criterion (3) of the set-colimit node now gives $[m,u]=[m,v]$, hence $[k,g]=[l,h]$. This proves faithfulness on each Hom set. The small filtered index needed here is the $J_{ij}$ checked in step 2.

proof.text: Conversely suppose the comparison is faithful. For g,g' : x → y in C_k with equal Phi_k-images, use representatives [k,T_kk(g)] and [k,T_kk(g')]. Naturality of theta_kk identifies their comparison images with Phi_k(g) and Phi_k(g'). Faithfulness gives equality of these classes. The model's homClass_eq_iff supplies a common later stage n where their homTransition images agree (both stage inequalities are propositionally equal). Naturality of tau_kkn identifies each transition of T_kk(g) with T_kn(g), and likewise for g'. Thus T_kn(g)=T_kn(g'), the Hom-inj condition. This uses the same diagonal-representative argument as the blueprint, with naturality replacing explicit transports through the normalization equalities.

proof.text: Combine the first three equivalences. Mathlib Functor.IsEquivalence is the Prop structure with Faithful, Full and EssSurj fields, so supply these fields from the three cocone conditions. Conversely, project these fields from an IsEquivalence proof and use the three equivalences to form CategoryCocone.IsFilteredTwoColimit. Functor.asEquivalence realizes this categorical criterion by an actual quasi-inverse if desired; no separate quasi-inverse Hom-bijection lemma is needed.
